title: AiiDA: automated interactive infrastructure and database for computational science
summary: AiiDA is an open-source Python infrastructure for computational materials science built on four pillars (Automation, Data, Environment, Sharing). It couples automated remote-job management with persistent storage, representing every calculation and data object as nodes in a directed acyclic graph to capture full provenance, and uses a SQL backend with a transitive-closure table for efficient graph/provenance queries. A daemon manages the calculation lifecycle (submit, monitor, retrieve, parse), a plugin interface supports new codes/data types, and a custom workflow engine encodes reusable multi-step pipelines, all aimed at reproducibility and data sharing.

title: Decision Provenance: Harnessing Data Flow for Accountable Systems
summary: This interdisciplinary (tech-legal) position paper proposes 'decision provenance' — using data-provenance methods to expose the decision pipelines (inputs, data flows, flow-on effects) of complex, interconnected algorithmic and automated systems-of-systems to improve accountability. It argues such provenance records support oversight, audit, GDPR compliance, liability/risk mitigation, and end-user empowerment, using ML pipelines as an illustrative case, and outlines capture mechanisms (disclosed vs observed), W3C PROV representation, trust, and retention as open challenges. It is a conceptual argument and research agenda rather than a built or evaluated system.

title: Provenance Data in the Machine Learning Lifecycle in Computational Science and Engineering
summary: The paper tackles provenance/lineage tracking across the full ML lifecycle in Computational Science and Engineering (data curation, learning data preparation, and learning), where heterogeneous domain and ML data are processed in multiple distributed workflows and manual tracking jeopardizes reproducibility. It contributes PROV-ML, a W3C PROV- and ML-Schema-compliant provenance data representation, and extends the ProvLake system (PLLib instrumentation, ProvTracker, ProvManager, query engine, Prov DBMS) to capture and query provenance with low overhead. It is validated in a real Oil & Gas seismic use case on 48 GPUs, reporting under 1% capture overhead and good weak scalability.

title: Vamsa: Automated Provenance Tracking in Data Science Scripts
summary: Vamsa introduces the ML provenance tracking problem: automatically determining which columns of a dataset were used to derive the features and labels of a trained ML model, motivated by fairness, bias, and explainability/regulatory needs. The system targets Python data-science scripts and automatically captures the data-to-model relationship without manual annotation. It addresses provenance/lineage as a data-management concern, using automated program analysis rather than an LLM-based agent.

title: AiiDA 1.0, a scalable computational infrastructure for automated reproducible workflows and data provenance
summary: AiiDA 1.0 is an open-source high-throughput infrastructure that automates the execution of complex computational workflows on local and remote/HPC resources while automatically recording the full data provenance of every calculation as a queryable directed graph in a relational database. It introduces a redesigned event-based engine (RabbitMQ daemon, scalable to tens of thousands of processes/hour), a Python workflow language with error handling and caching, a QueryBuilder for ORM-independent provenance queries, a REST API, and a plugin system/registry. The goal is automated, FAIR-compliant, reproducible data management for computational science, with provenance tracking as a first-class design principle.

title: Workflow Provenance in the Lifecycle of Scientific Machine Learning
summary: The paper proposes a workflow-provenance approach to build a holistic, queryable data view spanning the scientific-ML lifecycle (data curation, learning data preparation, learning). It contributes a lifecycle characterization and taxonomy, design principles with a W3C PROV/MLS-compliant representation (PROV-ML) and a distributed microservice reference architecture (ProvLake), and evaluates them in an Oil & Gas HPC case (393 nodes, 946 GPUs) showing <1% capture overhead, near-linear scalability, and up to an order-of-magnitude query acceleration. The focus is provenance/lineage tracking for reproducibility, explainability, and integrated data understanding rather than autonomous AI agents.

title: Provenance-Based Interpretation of Multi-Agent Information Analysis
summary: The paper presents a provenance-based system for interpreting and validating multi-agent information-analysis workflows, extending W3C PROV-O with a novel DIVE ontology that captures agents' appraisals, evidence, preferences, and nexuses over data. Using truth-maintenance-system (TMS) environments over a JanusGraph/TinkerPop PROV graph, it dynamically propagates confidence, supports counter-factual refutation, and indexes derivations by agents/sources/operation-classes to enable sensitivity, impact, and risk analysis, demonstrated in an interactive web-based validation UI on a fictional intelligence-analysis scenario. It targets data-integrity, provenance/lineage, and trust of conclusions flowing across autonomous agents in data-intensive pipelines.

title: EXSCLAIM! -- An automated pipeline for the construction of labeled materials imaging datasets from literature
summary: EXSCLAIM! is an automated Python pipeline that scrapes figure/caption pairs from open-source journals, separates compound figures into labeled master images using CV neural networks, and self-labels each image by distributing caption text and inferring hierarchical labels via Word2Vec and LDA topic modeling. It addresses the data-management problem of curating large, labeled scientific imaging datasets from literature where context is buried in captions. Evaluation reports figure-separator precision >0.80 (graphs ~0.98 at high threshold), ~87% joint microscopy/keyword accuracy, and a >280,000-image extracted dataset, prioritizing precision over recall under a data-abundance assumption.

title: Open-Science Platform for Computational Materials Science: AiiDA and the Materials Cloud
summary: The paper lays out a vision for an Open-Science Platform for computational materials science built on three pillars (open data generation, an accessible integration platform, and FAIR/DMP-compliant sharing), realized via the AiiDA infrastructure and the Materials Cloud portal. AiiDA is a Python platform following the ADES model (Automation, Data, Environment, Sharing) that uses a background daemon to automate HPC simulation submission and automatically records full provenance as directed acyclic graphs, enabling reproducibility, a-posteriori metadata tagging (e.g. TCOD ontology), and code-independent data export. Materials Cloud couples to AiiDA to support the full data lifecycle from learning and curated/raw data views to long-term archival with DOIs and OAI-PMH metadata, achieving FAIR compliance.

title: Software publications with rich metadata: state of the art, automated workflows and HERMES concept
summary: This HERMES concept paper (Helmholtz Metadata Collaboration) describes automated CI/CD-driven workflows that harvest existing software metadata from source repositories (CodeMeta, CITATION.cff, version control, platform APIs), validate and merge it into a coherent set resolving conflicts via source-precedence heuristics, and deposit it with rich metadata and persistent identifiers into publication repositories (InvenioRDM/Zenodo, Dataverse). It surveys the state of the art in software metadata types, formats, tooling, and publication workflows, then lays out a four-pipeline architecture (harvesting, processing, deposition, post-processing) implemented as reusable templates for GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, and Jenkins. The work is a concept/design paper soliciting community feedback rather than an evaluated system.

title: Scholarly Knowledge Extraction from Published Software Packages
summary: The paper proposes an automated pipeline that extracts machine-actionable scholarly knowledge from software packages published on Zenodo/GitHub. It combines the SOMEF metadata-extraction framework and the Zenodo/GitHub APIs to harvest software metadata and link packages to articles, then uses Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) static analysis of Python scripts to capture the input datasets, operations performed on data, and output datasets, filtering to 'scholarly' facts via keyword search in article full text and publishing the result as triples in the Open Research Knowledge Graph (ORKG).

title: AI-Enhanced Data Processing and Discovery Crowd Sourcing for Meteor Shower Mapping
summary: The paper describes the NASA CAMS meteor-surveillance project's move from manual data handling to an automated cloud-based pipeline that ingests, transfers, preprocesses, and classifies night-sky video detections from 600+ global cameras. A high-confidence BiLSTM classifier drives an active-learning loop that generates weak labels for a decade of unlabeled data, with human-in-the-loop review of low-confidence cases, drastically cutting manual annotation; a backend database, API, asynchronous job system, and interactive web portal support querying and visualization. The automation cleared a 3-4 month processing backlog and enabled discovery/validation of 200+ meteor showers.

title: Automated Annotation of Scientific Texts for ML-based Keyphrase Extraction and Validation
summary: The paper presents two semi-automated techniques for generating ground-truth text labels to validate ML-extracted keyphrase metadata for unlabeled scientific texts (JGI environmental-genomics proposals), removing the manual-labeling bottleneck that blocks automatic metadata curation. The first technique (artifact linkage) transfers human-curated keywords from linked publications (via Web of Science, PubMed, MeSH); the second (ontology-based annotation) matches proposal text against a curated application ontology (BERO, built from OBO ontologies) using NER tools (OGER, scispaCy) plus document-frequency ranking. Both feed the SciKey/ScienceSearch pipeline to evaluate YAKE-generated keywords, with artifact linkage validating ~44% of ML keywords vs ~23% for the ontology approach.

title: Facilitating the sharing of electrophysiology data analysis results through in-depth provenance capture
summary: The paper presents Alpaca (Automated Lightweight ProvenAnce CApture), a Python tool that automatically captures fine-grained provenance (inputs, outputs, function parameters, object metadata) during the execution of data-analysis scripts and serializes it as a W3C PROV / RDF sidecar file. It is demonstrated on an electrophysiology use case (computing mean PSDs from multichannel monkey motor-cortex recordings) to show how detailed data lineage makes analysis results reproducible, findable, and shareable per FAIR principles. The approach is automation via a function decorator plus a PROV-O-derived ontology, with NetworkX/GEXF graph visualization, rather than an LLM-based agent.

title: Recording provenance of workflow runs with RO-Crate
summary: The paper presents Workflow Run RO-Crate (WRROC), an extension of RO-Crate and Schema.org for packaging the prospective and retrospective provenance of computational workflow executions in a workflow-language- and system-agnostic way, organized into three layered profiles (Process, Workflow, Provenance Run Crate). It is aligned to W3C PROV via SKOS, implemented in a conversion tool (runcrate) and six workflow management systems (Galaxy, COMPSs, StreamFlow, WfExS, Sapporo, Autosubmit), and demonstrated on digital-pathology ML workflows including a successful re-execution. The work targets FAIR, traceability and reproducibility of scientific data products through automated, interoperable provenance recording.

title: Automated data processing and feature engineering for deep learning and big data applications: A survey
summary: This survey reviews techniques for automating data processing tasks in deep-learning and big-data pipelines, covering automated data preprocessing (cleaning, labeling, missing-data imputation, categorical encoding), data augmentation including generative-AI synthetic data, and feature engineering (extraction, construction, selection). It also covers AutoML methods that jointly optimize all stages of the ML pipeline. The work is classical/AutoML automation rather than LLM-agent based, and its data-management relevance lies in automating data-quality and data-preparation steps.

title: WaitGPT: Monitoring and Steering Conversational LLM Agent in Data Analysis with On-the-Fly Code Visualization
summary: WaitGPT is an interface that transforms a conversational LLM agent's generated data-analysis code into an on-the-fly, interactive flow diagram of data operations (load, filter, group, join, merge, aggregate, add column), letting users inspect runtime table states, verify steps, and steer/refine operations via direct manipulation or natural language without regenerating all the code. It is grounded in a formative study (N=8) of ChatGPT data-analysis users and evaluated in a within-subjects user study (N=12) against a code-only baseline. Findings show WaitGPT improved error-detection rates and user confidence in results, with lower cognitive load, though the diagram framing is HCI-centric and the data-management lifecycle is touched mainly via data wrangling and validation.

title: Automating Date Format Detection for Data Visualization
summary: The paper presents two automated algorithms - one based on minimum-description-length/minimum-entropy and one on NLP using a probabilistic context-free grammar with CYK parsing - that automatically infer date formats from string columns to streamline date parsing during data preparation for visualization tools and databases. On a 31K-record corpus the methods exceed ~90% accuracy, with the MDL approach being fast enough for interactive feedback and chosen for production, while the PCFG/NLP approach offers more flexibility for irregular formats. It is genuinely a data-quality/data-wrangling automation contribution but relies on classical pattern-recognition rather than AI agents or LLMs.

title: Enhancing Data Integrity through Provenance Tracking in Semantic Web Frameworks
summary: An industry applications paper from SURROUND/Encompass Australia describing a company-wide architecture for capturing data provenance and lineage across heterogeneous data-processing pipelines using the PROV-DM/PROV-O models, RDF, and Knowledge Graphs. Provenance is generated automatically by a Python workflow engine (ProvWF) with a reusable Block Library performing tasks like KG API calls, NLP/NER and ML classification, supplemented by human-in-the-loop review, and stored/visualized in the SURROUND Ontology Platform. Two project case studies illustrate how the approach addresses shared-entity identification and provenance granularity to improve data integrity, traceability and cross-system interoperability.

title: BiblioPage: A Dataset of Scanned Title Pages for Bibliographic Metadata Extraction
summary: BiblioPage is a dataset of ~2,118 scanned monograph title pages from 14 Czech libraries, each annotated with 16 structured bibliographic attributes (title, contributors, publication details) plus bounding boxes, built to enable automation of the otherwise manual metadata-digitization process in archives and libraries. The authors benchmark two AI approaches for automated metadata extraction: object detection (YOLO/DETR) combined with transformer OCR, and zero-shot Vision-LLMs (Llama 3.2-Vision, GPT-4o). GPT-4o with OCR achieved the best results (mF1 ~70), showing VLLMs benefit from semantic understanding for contributor roles while still struggling with title/subtitle and historical typefaces.

title: Text embedding models can be great data engineers
summary: ADEPT is an automated data-engineering pipeline that replaces conventional preprocessing, imputation, and feature-engineering steps with off-the-shelf LLM text embeddings applied to raw, text-serialized time series, refined by a Variational Information Bottleneck and a transformer classifier. It claims robustness to missing data, ill-formed records, corrupted formats, and irregular timestamps, and reports outperforming AutoML and domain-specific benchmarks across healthcare, finance, science, and IoT datasets. The contribution is automation of data-engineering effort rather than an autonomous/agentic data-management system.

title: MOLE: Metadata Extraction and Validation in Scientific Papers Using LLMs
summary: MOLE is a schema-driven framework that uses LLMs to automatically extract and validate ~32 dataset metadata attributes (license, volume, tasks, derived-from, access, etc.) from scientific papers across multiple languages, replacing manual annotation a la Masader. It introduces a 126-paper multilingual benchmark and systematically studies input format (LaTeX/PDF/Docling), few-shot prompting, web browsing, length constraints, and context length across 7 LLMs and 2 baselines. Findings: Gemini 2.5 Pro leads (75.23 avg), browsing improves precision, 3-shot helps, accessibility attributes are hardest, and LLMs still struggle with reliable length/structure enforcement.

title: Automatic Metadata Extraction for Text-to-SQL
summary: This AT&T CDO paper attacks the hardest part of text-to-SQL — understanding the database — by automatically generating field/table metadata instead of relying on expensive, often-stale SME annotations. It combines three extraction techniques (database profiling summarized by an LLM, query-log/query-plan mining of undocumented join paths and business-logic formulas, and LLM SQL-to-text few-shot generation) with a novel task-alignment schema-linking algorithm, achieving the #1 spot on the BIRD leaderboard. Findings: auto-profiled LLM metadata beats the human-supplied benchmark metadata, query logs surface ~25% more equality-join constraints than the documented schema, and effective schema linking remains a bottleneck.

title: Datasheets Aren't Enough: DataRubrics for Automated Quality Metrics and Accountability
summary: DataRubrics is a position paper plus tool that replaces descriptive datasheets/checklists with a structured, rubric-based framework of 10 measurable data-quality dimensions (sources, annotations, novelty, creation, utility, annotator guidelines, quality assurance, human/non-human language coverage, code). It operationalizes the rubric as an automated LLM-as-a-judge pipeline (OlmOCR text extraction, R3-Qwen reward-model filtering of dataset/benchmark papers, then GPT-4.1-mini scoring with reasoning + paper-section references via constrained structured decoding), validated against expert human annotations on 100 NeurIPS papers and applied to trend analyses across NeurIPS/ICLR/ICML/ACL/EMNLP/LREC/CVPR/Interspeech (2021-2024). The goal is scalable, reproducible dataset-quality assessment to aid authors and reviewers as submission volumes surge.

title: AssistedDS: Benchmarking How External Domain Knowledge Assists LLMs in Automated Data Science
summary: AssistedDS is a benchmark that tests whether LLMs (GPT-4o/o4-mini/4o-mini, Claude 3.5 Haiku, Gemini 2.0 Flash, DeepSeek-chat) can critically use external domain knowledge when generating end-to-end code for tabular prediction tasks, using synthetic datasets with known generative mechanisms plus real Kaggle competitions, each bundled with curated helpful and adversarial documents on data cleaning, feature engineering, and model selection. It finds LLMs uncritically adopt provided hints, suffering large predictive-performance drops under adversarial content, that helpful guidance cannot offset adversarial influence, and that on Kaggle data they systematically mishandle time-series, feature-engineering consistency, and categorical/non-numeric variables. The work argues for knowledge-aware automated data science systems that can critically filter external expert knowledge like a human data scientist.

title: Semantic-Aware Parsing for Security Logs
summary: Matryoshka is an end-to-end system that uses LLMs to automatically generate semantically-aware, deterministic log parsers from unlabeled log lines, with no human labels or intervention. It works in three stages — syntax parsing (a parse tree of templates with regexes), semantic schema creation (consistent variable naming/descriptions), and mapping fields to standardized security taxonomies (OCSF/UDM) — using an alternating generate/validate loop where validation is framed as sandboxed code editing. Evaluated on a new SecurityLogs corpus, LogHub2.0, and 27 real-world Google SecOps log types, it matches or beats expert-written parsers on query precision/recall while removing the manual parser-writing burden.

title: AI Model Passport: Data and System Traceability Framework for Transparent AI in Health
summary: The paper proposes the AI Model Passport, a standardized, machine-interpretable provenance/metadata framework that gives AI models and datasets a verifiable digital identity and traces them across the full lifecycle (data collection, curation, dataset specification, training/evaluation, production). It is implemented as AIPassport, an open-source MLOps tool that automates metadata capture via MLflow autologging, DVC/Git versioning, and MINIO storage, grounded in W3C PROV, DCAT(-AP/HealthDCAT-AP), MLS, DPV and PMLM ontologies. Validated as a proof-of-concept on a prostate-cancer lesion-segmentation use case in the ProCAncer-I EU project (14,300+ patients).

title: Provenance Tracking in Large-Scale Machine Learning Systems
summary: The paper introduces yProv4ML, a library for collecting provenance data from large-scale ML training in JSON format compliant with W3C PROV and PROV-ML standards, integrated with the broader yProv framework and extensible via plugins. It targets reproducibility, lineage tracking, and energy/efficiency analysis of ML workflows, demonstrated on a MODIS foundation-model scaling study at Oak Ridge. It is provenance/lineage tooling (classical automation) for the ML lifecycle rather than an autonomous AI-agent system, so the agent angle is weak but the provenance/data-management angle is genuine.

title: Exploring LLM Capabilities in Extracting DCAT-Compatible Metadata for Data Cataloging
summary: This study evaluates how well autoregressive LLMs (Llama 3.1/3.2, Gemini 1.5 Flash/Pro, GPT-4o/4o-Mini) can automatically generate eight DCAT-compatible metadata properties (title, description, creator, language, spatial, issued, keyword, theme) for text-based documents to support data cataloging, comparing zero-shot, few-shot, and fine-tuned approaches against human-curated ground truth across nine datasets. It finds LLMs can produce metadata comparable to human content—especially for semantic tasks—with larger models and fine-tuning improving accuracy, and proposes a tiered strategy matching model size/family to task complexity. The work positions LLMs as a faster, reliable aid for metadata maintenance while stressing the need for expert oversight in sensitive domains.

title: ArchiveGPT: A human-centered evaluation of using a vision language model for image cataloguing
summary: ArchiveGPT uses an out-of-the-box vision language model (InternVL2-Llama3-76B) with few-shot prompting and a FAIR/LIDO-aligned catalogue template to automatically draft metadata descriptions for archaeological photographic prints from the LEIZA archive. A preregistered human-centered experiment had archive/archaeology experts and non-experts classify AI- vs expert-written descriptions, rate accuracy/usefulness, and report trust and willingness to adopt. Findings: detection was above chance, OCR errors and hallucinations hurt perceived quality, experts were more hesitant to adopt over preservation-responsibility concerns, and the authors advocate AI-as-draft-generator subordinate to human verification.

title: PROV-AGENT: Unified Provenance for Tracking AI Agent Interactions in Agentic Workflows
summary: PROV-AGENT is a provenance model that extends W3C PROV and incorporates Model Context Protocol (MCP) concepts to capture agent-centric metadata (prompts, responses, model invocations, agent decisions) and relate it to traditional workflow tasks and data in a single, queryable end-to-end lineage graph. It is implemented on top of the open-source Flowcept observability framework (using @flowcept_agent_tool and FlowceptLLM decorators) and evaluated on a cross-facility edge-cloud-HPC additive-manufacturing workflow, enabling root-cause queries that trace hallucinated/erroneous agent decisions back through prompts, model outputs, and source data. The goal is transparency, reproducibility, and reliability of agentic workflows so errors can be traced and mitigated.

title: AdProv: A Method for Provenance of Process Adaptations
summary: AdProv is a method-engineering contribution that defines how to collect, store, retrieve, and visualize the provenance of runtime adaptations to business and scientific workflows, an aspect prior provenance tooling neglected. It introduces a change-event data model, an Adaptation extension to the XES standard, a mapping to PROV-O/PROV-DM, and a Provenance Holder service architecture; where execution environments don't emit explicit change events, it reuses process mining / anomaly / change-drift detection to identify adaptations automatically. Feasibility is argued through a worked online-shopping workflow example visualized with ProvToolbox, with future work on trusted collaborative cross-organizational adaptation provenance.

title: InferA: A Smart Assistant for Cosmological Ensemble Data
summary: InferA is a LangChain/LangGraph multi-agent system that lets users query and analyze terabyte-to-petabyte cosmology ensemble data (HACC simulations) in natural language without full data ingestion. A supervisor agent orchestrates specialized agents for planning, RAG-based metadata/column extraction, data loading into DuckDB, SQL/Python/visualization code generation, a sandboxed quality-assurance loop, and complete provenance tracking; it was evaluated over 200 runs (20 questions x 10) across difficulty levels plus an 11.2 TB scalability case study. The work targets ingest, metadata interpretation, data quality, and provenance/reproducibility stages of the data-management lifecycle.

title: Metadata Extraction Leveraging Large Language Models
summary: A Box AI Platform paper presenting an end-to-end LLM-enhanced pipeline for extracting structured metadata (salient legal clauses, parties, dates, governing law) from contracts. The system combines OCR/text conversion (Azure Document Intelligence), novel NER-enhanced Borda re-ranking and a neural model-based chunk re-ranker for strategic chunk selection, and LLM synthesis using Chain-of-Thought prompting plus structured tool/JSON calling, evaluated on CUAD and a proprietary lease dataset. It adds an LLM-as-judge layer for label correction (raising F1 above the base agent) and privacy-preserving online quality monitoring dashboards.

title: Towards Defect Phase Diagrams: From Research Data Management to Automated Workflows
summary: The paper describes a comprehensive research data management system built for a materials-science Collaborative Research Centre, combining the openBIS ELN/LIMS with a custom Streamlit companion application. It automates ingest from cloud object storage, extraction of metadata from heterogeneous proprietary instrument file formats, parent-child provenance tracking, controlled vocabularies/validation for data quality, and Python-scripted automated reports and baseline analyses. The automation is classical (scheduled Python jobs, parsers, web app) rather than AI-agent-based, but it directly targets multiple data-management lifecycle stages.

title: Knowledge Graphs Generation from Cultural Heritage Texts: Combining LLMs and Ontological Engineering for Scholarly Debates
summary: ATR4CH is a five-step methodology for coordinating LLM-based knowledge extraction with Cultural Heritage ontologies (the SEBI ontology) to convert unstructured scholarly texts into queryable RDF knowledge graphs, validated on a case study of authenticity/forgery debates from Wikipedia. It implements a sequential pipeline using three LLMs (Claude Sonnet 3.7, Llama 3.3 70B, GPT-4o-mini) for tasks including metadata extraction, scholarly entity recognition, evidence extraction, hypothesis extraction, and discourse representation with RDF-star reification and PROV-O provenance. Reported results show strong metadata/evidence extraction (0.96-0.99 and 0.95-0.97 F1) and weaker discourse representation (0.62 G-EVAL), with smaller models performing competitively for cost-effective deployment.

title: Identifying and extracting Data Access Statements from full-text academic articles
summary: CORE describes a dashboard module that automatically identifies and extracts Data Access Statements (DAS) from full-text academic articles, encoding them as a standard metadata component to reduce manual curation effort for repository managers. The approach uses keyword-matching over full text to narrow candidate papers, then a regex-based scoring system to confirm a genuine DAS and extract the dataset URL, surfaced in a review/correct UI and via an API for deposit-time integration. It targets metadata enrichment, funder-compliance monitoring, and data discoverability/reuse in the scholarly repository ecosystem.

title: From Show Programmes to Data: Designing a Workflow to Make Performing Arts Ephemera Accessible Through Language Models
summary: The paper presents an end-to-end workflow that transforms underused performing-arts ephemera (theatre programmes from the Festival d'Avignon) into structured, interoperable metadata. It chains document segmentation, a vision-language model (Claude Sonnet 3.7) for transcription (>98% extraction accuracy), a custom Linked Art ontology extension for performing arts, and a small RL-trained reasoning model (POntAvignon) that generates Wikidata-aligned RDF triples. It is positioned as an early example of ontology-driven, explainable metadata generation for the digital humanities, with the goal of building large-scale interoperable cultural-heritage data.

title: Beyond Text-to-SQL: Autonomous Research-Driven Database Exploration with DAR
summary: DAR (Data Agnostic Researcher) is a hierarchical multi-agent system built on Google ADK that autonomously explores BigQuery relational databases without human-initiated queries, spanning three layers: initialization (intent inference + metadata/schema extraction), execution (SQL and BigQuery-native generative-AI query synthesis with iterative validation), and synthesis (report generation with a quality-control escalation loop). All reasoning runs inside BigQuery via native AI functions (AI.GENERATE, ML.GENERATE_TEXT) to avoid data movement and preserve governance. In a case study on an asset-incident dataset, DAR finished end-to-end analysis in 16 minutes vs 7h10m for human analysts (~27x faster), trading interpretive depth for rapid first-pass exploration.

title: AI4EOSC: a Federated Cloud Platform for Artificial Intelligence in Scientific Research
summary: AI4EOSC is a federated, open-source cloud platform operationalizing the full AI/ML lifecycle (development, training, serverless inference, federated learning) within the European Open Science Cloud. Its DM-relevant core is a 'FAIR-by-design' framework: a Jenkins CI/CD pipeline that automatically validates user-defined metadata against a schema, serializes it via MLDCAT-AP for semantic interoperability, and non-intrusively assembles W3C PROV-compliant provenance/lineage graphs (RDF/JSON-LD via RML/CARML mappings) linking code, datasets, weights, and training runs. It is validated as a real deployment across three EOSC community projects (iMagine, KMD4EOSC, AI4Life) plus scalability and training-overhead benchmarks.

title: Clinical Document Metadata Extraction: A Scoping Review
summary: A PRISMA-ScR scoping review (67 of 266 screened articles, 2011-2025) cataloging methods, datasets, and applications for extracting clinical document metadata (document type, section/structure, medical specialty, author role, encounter setting) from unstructured EHR text. It traces a three-phase methodological evolution from rule-based and feature-engineered traditional ML to transformer-based models (BERT/BioBERT/ClinicalBERT) and, recently, LLMs, and notes a persistent scarcity of public corpora plus heterogeneous, custom institutional schemas that drive demand for data-harmonization solutions. The work is a survey/critique of automated metadata extraction rather than a system, with no autonomous agents involved.

title: SciDataCopilot: An Agentic Data Preparation Framework for AGI-driven Scientific Discovery
summary: SciDataCopilot is a staged four-agent framework (Data Access, Intent Parsing, Data Processing, Data Integration) that turns natural-language scientific intent and heterogeneous raw experimental files into 'Scientific AI-Ready' datasets. It autonomously explores data directories to build a normalized metadata knowledge base (data/tool/case lakes), retrieves and adapts reusable cases into verified processing plans, runs self-repairing code-execution loops with traceable artifacts, and applies constraint-driven cross-modal integration. Evaluated on three domains (enzyme catalysis, EEG/MEG neuroscience, Earth/meteorology), it matches human-expert quality while delivering up to 30x speedups and large-scale curation (214K enzyme reaction records).

title: CausalAgent: A Conversational Multi-Agent System for End-to-End Causal Inference
summary: CausalAgent is a conversational multi-agent system (MAS + RAG + MCP, GLM-4.6 backbone) that automates end-to-end causal inference from a natural-language query, spanning data cleaning, causal structure learning, bias correction, and report generation. Within the pipeline, a dedicated Data Processing Agent handles preprocessing (file validation, summary statistics, missing-rate and unique-value checks, variable-meaning inference) and quality detection, producing a 'causal analysis friendliness' rating plus profiling visualizations (histograms, correlation heatmaps). The system is demonstrated as a case study on the Sachs protein-signaling dataset rather than benchmarked, with data quality/profiling being one component subordinate to the causal-inference goal.

title: News Harvesting from Google News combining Web Scraping, LLM Metadata Extraction and SCImago Media Rankings enrichment: a case study of IFMIF-DONES
summary: This paper develops and evaluates a five-stage automated pipeline that builds a news dataset from Google News by combining Selenium-based web scraping, local LLM (Mistral-NeMo-12b) metadata extraction, and SCImago Media Rankings enrichment, using the IFMIF-DONES fusion project as a case study. Across 81 region-language combinations and 737 scripts it yielded 1,482 validated records (56% noise reduction) with high complementarity (76% exclusive) versus two licensed press databases. It reports that LLMs extract structured fields (titles, body) reliably but hallucinate fabricated placeholder text when content is inaccessible, requiring string-matching validation, and points to agentic browser tools (Cowork) as a more robust future ingestion approach.

title: Audiocards: Structured Metadata Improves Audio Language Models For Sound Design
summary: The paper proposes 'audiocards', multi-field structured metadata (nouns/verbs, UCS taxonomy categories, adjectives, captions) for sound effects libraries, generated by few-shot prompting an off-the-shelf LLM over available file metadata plus computed audio descriptors. Because sound-library metadata is often missing or incomplete and costly to add manually, they automate enrichment and show that training downstream audio captioners and text-audio retrieval models on audiocards improves metadata generation, captioning, and search over baselines and state-of-the-art audio LLMs. They also fine-tune a DistilBERT classifier to assign UCS taxonomy categories (96% held-out accuracy) and release a 500-file human-verified audiocard evaluation set.

title: Automated Extraction of Mechanical Constitutive Models from Scientific Literature using Large Language Models: Applications in Cultural Heritage Conservation
summary: The paper presents a two-stage agentic LLM framework that mines unstructured scientific PDFs to build a structured database of mechanical constitutive models for cultural-heritage materials. A cost-efficient 'Gatekeeper' agent filters ~2,000 papers for relevance and a high-capability 'Analyst' agent performs fine-grained extraction with context-aware symbolic grounding and schema-constrained JSON decoding, yielding 185 model instances and 450+ calibrated parameters at 80.4% precision. The result is exposed through a web platform supporting automated ingestion and semantic retrieval, cutting manual curation effort by ~90% in a human-in-the-loop workflow.

title: SIDEKICK: A Semantically Integrated Resource for Drug Effects, Indications, and Contraindications
summary: SIDEKICK is a drug-safety knowledge graph built with an automated LLM-based extraction + Graph-Retrieval-Augmented-Generation workflow that ingests 50,000+ FDA Structured Product Labels, extracts indications/contraindications/adverse reactions, and standardizes them by mapping to the HPO, MONDO, and RxNorm ontologies, serialized as RDF under the SIO upper-level ontology with provenance links back to source documents. The pipeline (Gemini 2.5 Flash extraction, embedding + graph-traversal ontology mapping, BioBERT NER for drug entities, ShEx/ELK validation) produced 3.16M triples and 205k clinical associations. It outperforms OnSIDES (AUC 0.7174 vs 0.6612) on drug-target prediction by side-effect similarity, demonstrating that ontology-based curation improves downstream reasoning.

title: CourtGuard: A Model-Agnostic Framework for Zero-Shot Policy Adaptation in LLM Safety
summary: CourtGuard is a retrieval-augmented multi-agent framework (Attacker, Defender, Judge agents grounded in retrieved policy documents) that reimagines LLM safety evaluation as an 'Evidentiary Debate' decoupled from model weights, achieving SOTA on safety benchmarks and zero-shot adaptation to new policies without fine-tuning. Beyond safety classification, the authors use the agent as a high-fidelity automated annotator to curate and audit nine adversarial-attack datasets and to uncover label noise in existing benchmarks (e.g., JailJudge, HarmBench), positioning it as an automated data auditor/curator that reduces human labeling burden. The data-management angle (automated curation, data-quality auditing, policy/governance grounding via GDPR and MLCommons) is a demonstrated secondary capability rather than the central thesis.

title: CiteAudit: You Cited It, But Did You Read It? A Benchmark for Verifying Scientific References in the LLM Era
summary: CiteAudit is a benchmark and SOP-driven multi-agent framework for detecting hallucinated/erroneous scientific citations in the LLM era. A pipeline of specialized agents (Extractor, Memory, Web Search, Judge, Scholar) parses citation strings into structured metadata, checks consistency against authoritative scholarly records, and emits a real/fake judgment plus a fine-grained mismatch (title/author/venue/year/identifier) provenance report. Evaluated on a 6k+ citation benchmark (generated perturbations + human-validated real-world errors), it beats commercial and open-source LLM baselines on F1 while being cheaper than top proprietary models.

title: From Static Repositories to Agentic Knowledge Webs: ResearchTwin and the S-Index for Federated Human-AI Research Discovery
summary: ResearchTwin is an open-source federated platform that aggregates a researcher's papers, code, and datasets from multiple scholarly APIs into a conversational digital twin, and introduces the S-index, a FAIR-grounded composite metric (Quality gate + reuse Impact + Collaboration) that scores datasets/code reuse alongside citations. It exposes an inter-agentic discovery API using Schema.org types, HATEOAS navigation, and an official MCP server so AI agents can autonomously discover and traverse research artifacts and cross-lab synergies. Evaluation is a preliminary deployed prototype: a two-researcher case study showing the S-index discriminates impact profiles that the H-index treats identically, plus endpoint latency measurements.

title: Agentics 2.0: Logical Transduction Algebra for Agentic Data Workflows
summary: Agentics 2.0 is a Python-native framework that formalizes LLM inference as typed 'transducible functions' (a logical transduction algebra) so agentic workflows over structured data are schema-validated, explainable via evidence/provenance tracing, and scalable through stateless async Map-Reduce. The authors instantiate reusable design patterns and evaluate on DiscoveryBench (data-driven hypothesis discovery over CSV datasets) and Archer (NL-to-SQL semantic parsing), reporting state-of-the-art-competitive scores. The DM relevance comes from operating directly over CSVs/databases, parsing dataframes into typed schemas via canonical transduction, and carrying per-slot provenance/confidence across the pipeline.

title: VDCook:DIY video data cook your MLLMs
summary: VDCook is a self-evolving video data 'operating system' that lets researchers request in-domain video datasets via natural-language queries plus parameters (scale, retrieval-synthesis ratio, quality threshold). A query-optimization agent expands queries, an MCP-based crawler ingests and periodically re-crawls web video alongside user uploads, and a Model Annotation Center enriches each clip with multi-dimensional metadata (scene segmentation, motion scoring, OCR ratio, captions) before policy filtering, provenance tracking, and packaging into reproducible manifests/notebooks. It reframes dataset construction from a static one-shot release into a continuously evolving, governance-enabled ecosystem with a data-model co-evolution loop including synthetic long-tail augmentation.

title: Omics Data Discovery Agents
summary: The paper presents an agentic framework that mines PubMed Central omics articles and transforms unstructured literature into searchable, computable research objects. LLM agents (with separated-concern, prompt-injection-aware design) extract metadata, identify and download published datasets, and invoke containerized quantification pipelines (MaxQuant, DIA-NN) exposed via Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, then perform cross-study synthesis. Evaluation on 39 proteomics papers shows ~80% precision for repository dataset identification and ~63% overlap in differentially expressed proteins when matching reported preprocessing.

title: Design and evaluation of an agentic workflow for crisis-related synthetic tweet datasets
summary: The paper proposes an agentic workflow with three roles (generator, compliance evaluator, feedback augmenter) that iteratively produces crisis-related synthetic tweet datasets conditioned on target labels (location, damage level), accepting only tweets that pass heuristic compliance checks for label correctness and textual diversity. Applied to post-earthquake damage assessment across six real earthquake events, it shows the synthetic datasets capture target labels and serve as a usable proxy for evaluating AI systems on geolocalization and damage-level prediction. It addresses the data-curation bottleneck created by restricted Twitter/X API access and costly manual annotation.

title: Data Darwinism Part II: DataEvolve -- AI can Autonomously Evolve Pretraining Data Curation
summary: DataEvolve is a closed-loop, multi-agent LLM framework (data observer, strategy designer, data cleaner, quality judge) that autonomously evolves per-category data-curation/cleaning strategies for LLM pretraining corpora, replacing manual expert-designed strategies. Applied to 8 academic categories spanning 672B tokens of Nemotron-CC, it produces Darwin-CC (504B tokens); 3B models trained on it beat raw data by +3.96 points and surpass DCLM, Ultra-FineWeb, and FineWeb-Edu across 18 benchmarks. Analysis shows evolved strategies converge on cleaning-focused operations (noise removal, format normalization, domain-aware preservation) rather than content rewriting, and ablations confirm iterative evolution is essential.

title: Prose2Policy (P2P): A Practical LLM Pipeline for Translating Natural-Language Access Policies into Executable Rego
summary: Prose2Policy (P2P) is a modular, LLM-based pipeline that converts natural-language access control policies (NLACPs) into executable Rego (Open Policy Agent) code, chaining policy detection, component extraction (decision/subject/action/resource/condition/purpose), schema validation, Rego generation, linting (Regal), and automatic positive/negative unit-test generation and execution. Evaluated on the ACRE dataset (485 statements, 389 accepted), it reached a 95.3% compile rate, 82.2% positive-test and 98.9% negative-test pass rates, outperforming rule-based test generation. The work targets auditable, deployment-ready governance for Zero Trust and compliance-driven environments rather than guaranteeing identical outputs across runs.

title: Autonomous Agent-Orchestrated Digital Twins (AADT): Leveraging the OpenClaw Framework for State Synchronization in Rare Genetic Disorders
summary: The paper proposes AADT, an autonomous agent-orchestrated framework that uses the OpenClaw local-first AI agent runtime (with a scheduled 'heartbeat' polling cycle and modular Agent Skills) to keep medical digital twins for rare genetic disorders continuously synchronized. A custom skill (PhenoSnap/PhenoSkill) deterministically ingests caregiver free-text to extract timestamped HPO phenotype terms (with PII redaction and negation handling) and monitors ClinVar monthly for variant reclassifications, reassembling a unified digital-twin JSON state with full event-sourced provenance. The LLM is restricted to orchestration while all clinical data extraction/transformation runs through deterministic, version-controlled tools to prevent hallucination from entering the data state.

title: Compliance-by-Construction Argument Graphs: Using Generative AI to Produce Evidence-Linked Formal Arguments for Certification-Grade Accountability
summary: The paper proposes a compliance-by-construction architecture in which GenAI (with RAG) drafts formal 'argument graph' fragments (claims-reasoning-evidence, inspired by assurance cases/GSN) that a deterministic validation kernel must approve before they enter an official decision record, with a W3C PROV-aligned provenance ledger capturing models, prompts, retrieval sets, and human edits for full auditability. The kernel enforces invariants such as evidence completeness, evidence admissibility within data-governance scope, rule coverage, non-contradiction, and provenance completeness, so unsupported/hallucinated claims are rejected rather than persisted. It is a design + evaluation-strategy paper (worked examples and enforceable invariants), aimed at certification-grade accountability for high-stakes AI decision systems under regimes like the EU AI Act.

title: From PDF to RAG-Ready: Evaluating Document Conversion Frameworks for Domain-Specific Question Answering
summary: This paper systematically benchmarks four open-source PDF-to-Markdown conversion frameworks (Docling, MinerU, Marker, DeepSeek OCR) by their downstream impact on RAG question-answering accuracy, across 21 configurations varying conversion tool, cleaning transformations, chunking strategy, and metadata enrichment, over a 1706-page Portuguese military HR corpus. Built as a Medallion-style ETL pipeline (Bronze/Silver/Gold) with a configuration-driven ingestion orchestrator, it finds that data-preparation quality dominates RAG performance: Docling with hierarchy-aware chunking plus VLM image descriptions reached 94.1%, surpassing even manual curation, while a naive GraphRAG layer underperformed (82%). The work positions upstream data ingestion/structuring as the primary lever for reliable RAG, more impactful than swapping retrievers or LLMs.

title: Pioneer Agent: Continual Improvement of Small Language Models in Production
summary: Pioneer Agent is a closed-loop, Claude-Sonnet-orchestrated LangGraph system that autonomously runs the small-LM fine-tuning lifecycle, treating data curation as a first-class search dimension alongside hyperparameters and learning strategy. Its production mode is essentially automated data management over inference-log datasets: it ingests judged failure traces via SQL, builds a failure taxonomy, confirms weaknesses through targeted probing, filters poisonous vs. fixable noise, synthesizes corrective curricula (gold/hard-negative/replay slices under explicit quality controls), and retrains under regression gates, while persisting a data-curation.md provenance/lineage log. Evaluated on eight cold-start benchmarks and the new AdaptFT-Bench plus two production deployments, it improves over base models by 1.6-83.8 points and avoids the regressions naive retraining suffers under accumulating data noise.

title: Tracing the Roots: A Multi-Agent Framework for Uncovering Data Lineage in Post-Training LLMs
summary: The paper introduces 'data lineage' for the LLM post-training dataset ecosystem and proposes an automated multi-agent framework (sourcing, extracting, tracing, and aggregation agents over LangChain with GPT-5.1 and Gemini-2.5) that mines unstructured documentation (HuggingFace READMEs, GitHub, arXiv papers) to reconstruct an evolutionary graph of 430 datasets connected by 971 inheritance edges. Using the lineage graph the authors diagnose structural redundancy (e.g., open-instruct-v1 at 46.48%) and trace benchmark-contamination propagation (e.g., Caco-1.3M inheriting 37.95% of Omni-Math), then leverage root-node provenance sampling to build a more diverse 570K-instruction post-training corpus that beats larger baselines on Vendi Score. It positions lineage-centric topological analysis as an efficient, drift-robust alternative to sample-level dataset comparison.

title: Multi-Task LLM with LoRA Fine-Tuning for Automated Cancer Staging and Biomarker Extraction
summary: The paper fine-tunes Llama-3-8B-Instruct with LoRA, repurposed as a discriminative encoder with parallel classification heads, to extract TNM staging, histologic grade, and ER/PR/HER2 biomarkers from unstructured breast-cancer pathology reports, framed as automating large-scale cancer-registry data curation. Trained on 10,677 expert-verified reports (labels bootstrapped via a human-in-the-loop regex engine), it reaches Macro F1 0.976, beating rule-based NLP, zero-shot LLMs, and single-task baselines while enforcing schema adherence and avoiding generative hallucination. It is relevant to the curation/structured-extraction stage of the data lifecycle, but it is supervised ML rather than an AI agent (no tools, planning, or autonomy).

title: BranchBench: Aligning Database Branching with Agentic Demands
summary: BranchBench is a benchmark for evaluating branchable relational databases under agentic workloads, where autonomous agents fork, mutate, evaluate, and discard speculative database branches. It characterizes five workloads including data curation/cleaning (agents detecting/correcting data-quality errors via branch-mutate-validate loops), failure reproduction, software engineering, MCTS, and simulation, and benchmarks Neon, Dolt, TigerData, Xata, and PostgreSQL. It finds a fundamental tension where systems optimized for fast branching suffer 5-4000x slower reads while fast-data systems incur 25-1500x higher branch-creation latency, and no current system supports the workloads at scale.

title: PrismaDV: Automated Task-Aware Data Unit Test Generation
summary: PrismaDV is a compound AI (LLM-based, DSPy-implemented) system that generates task-aware data unit tests by jointly analyzing dataset profiles and the code of downstream tasks to detect column-access patterns, infer implicit data assumptions, and synthesize executable pydeequ/Great-Expectations-style constraints. It adds SIFTA, a prompt-optimization procedure that uses scarce constraint/task execution outcomes (via 'failure precision' backtracking) to adapt prompts over time. On two new benchmarks (ICDBench, EIDBench; 60 tasks across five datasets) it beats task-agnostic tools (Deequ, TFDV), zero/few-shot LLM prompting, and agentic baselines (PocketFlow, SWE-Agent) by >20 F1 points, and SIFTA outperforms a generic prompt optimizer (GEPA).

title: Governed Collaborative Memory as Artificial Selection in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
summary: This Viewpoint frames the question of which candidate agent memories should become durable, shared institutional state as 'governed collaborative memory' — a selection regime over persistent memory in LLM-based multi-agent systems. It proposes a four-layer memory architecture (agent-local, shared institutional, archive, project-continuity) with provenance and version lineage that make selection auditable, distinguishes four selection regimes (ungoverned, constitutional/hybrid, automatic metric-based, human-ratified), and illustrates them with documented traces from one running ecosystem. The contribution is a design agenda arguing that agent memory should be evaluated not just for recall/performance but for provenance fidelity, selection traceability, epistemic quality, correction pathways, and role preservation.

title: AegisTS: A Hierarchical Agent System with Reinforcement Learning for Multivariate Time Series Data Cleaning
summary: AegisTS is a hierarchical reinforcement-learning agent system for cleaning multivariate time series that suffer from co-occurring quality issues (missing values, outliers, constraint violations). A high-level agent prioritizes which quality issue to fix while a low-level agent selects the specific cleaning operator, and a dual-stage reward (lightweight proxy model for dense feedback plus a complex downstream model for sparse terminal reward) lets the system construct an effective dataset-specific cleaning pipeline without ground truth. Across four real-world datasets it outperforms cleaning baselines (EDITOR, Clean4TSDB, DiffPrep, sampling) on upstream and downstream metrics, reporting up to 96% cleaning-quality and 27% downstream improvement.

title: Dynamic Authorization for Knowledge-Base Agents in 6G
summary: A short conceptual paper proposing a hybrid authorization framework for multi-agent systems accessing shared Knowledge Bases in 6G, combining roles with First-Order-Logic predicates to enforce zero-trust, triple-level (Subject-Predicate-Object) access control over knowledge-graph metadata. It eliminates RBAC permission inheritance, embeds the Policy Decision Point in the logical reasoner for continuous query-time enforcement, blocks ontology 'crawling' via wildcard/variable-predicate protection, and supports instant session revocation by purging an agent's authorization graph. The data-management angle is governance/access control over the metadata that autonomous agents are allowed to read.

title: Securing the Agent: Vendor-Neutral, Multitenant Enterprise Retrieval and Tool Use
summary: The paper formalizes the 'relevance-authorization gap' in multitenant agentic RAG systems, where retrieval ranks documents by relevance rather than authorization, causing one tenant's confidential data to surface to another. It proposes a layered isolation architecture (policy-aware ingestion with tenant ownership metadata, retrieval-time ABAC gating, and shared inference) enforced through server-side orchestration, validated via the open-source OGX framework with an OpenAI-compatible Responses API. Empirically, ABAC gating eliminates cross-tenant leakage (CTLR/AVR to 0%) and blocks all prompt-injection probes at the retrieval layer, with only ~19ms overhead.

title: Partial Evidence Bench: Benchmarking Authorization-Limited Evidence in Agentic Systems
summary: Partial Evidence Bench is a deterministic benchmark that measures a governance-critical failure of enterprise agents operating over scoped, ACL-partitioned corpora: producing a complete-seeming answer even when material evidence lies outside the caller's authorization boundary (without flagging the gap). It ships three scenario families (due diligence, compliance audit, security incident response) totaling 72 synthetic tasks with oracle complete/authorized-view answers and gap-report oracles, scoring systems on answer correctness, completeness awareness, gap-report quality, and unsafe completeness. Baselines show silent filtering is catastrophically unsafe across all families while explicit fail-and-report eliminates unsafe completeness, and preliminary multi-model runs (Claude variants, GPT-4o, Llama) show model- and scenario-dependent over/under-claiming behavior.

title: Data Language Models: A New Foundation Model Class for Tabular Data
summary: The paper introduces the Data Language Model (DLM) as a new foundation-model class for tabular data and presents Schema-1, a 140M-parameter model trained on 2.3M datasets that ingests raw cell values, per-column distributional summaries, column semantics, and missingness structure without any preprocessing pipeline. Beyond row-level prediction, Schema-1 performs native missing-value imputation (beating classical methods and frontier LLMs) and blind dataset sector classification across 10,000 industry sectors from raw cells alone (91.4% top-1), positioned as the substrate on which vertical AI applications and autonomous agents over enterprise data are built. The DM relevance lies in automating data-quality (imputation), metadata/domain identification, and the elimination of cleaning/encoding pipelines, though the agentic use is aspirational rather than implemented.

title: TCMIIES: A Browser-Based LLM-Powered Intelligent Information Extraction System for Academic Literature
summary: TCMIIES is a browser-based, zero-installation single-page application that uses commercial LLM APIs to extract structured information from academic literature (demonstrated on Traditional Chinese Medicine papers). Its core is a schema-guided prompting framework that auto-generates system prompts from user-defined fields via a GUI, plus rule-based field mapping for Chinese databases (CNKI/Wanfang), concurrent batch processing with retries, and JSON parsing/validation, achieving >94% JSON output compliance and ~81.6% field-level extraction accuracy. It is positioned as a privacy-preserving, no-code tool to turn unstructured papers into structured records for literature surveys and meta-research.

title: Governing AI-Assisted Security Operations: A Design Science Framework for Operational Decision Support
summary: A design-science study proposing a 'governed AI query broker' that separates AI planning from execution when LLMs/RAG/coding agents access privileged security telemetry (KQL over Microsoft Defender XDR/Sentinel/ADX). The broker enforces schema-grounded retrieval, approved parameterized templates, policy validation, least-privilege read-only adapters, threat-intelligence provenance, auditable agent traces, and engineering-review-board promotion gates so AI-generated queries stay accountable, cost-controlled, schema-valid, and auditable. The contribution is a management framework with six design propositions, a maturity model, role/accountability model, and a staged evaluation protocol — not a new query technique or detection algorithm.

title: Autonomous FAIR Digital Objects: From Passive Assertions to Active Knowledge
summary: The paper operationalizes Autonomous FAIR Digital Objects (aFDOs), which augment passive FAIR Digital Objects with embedded, standards-aligned (RDF-star, PROV-O, SHACL, ODRL, ActivityStreams 2.0) condition-action policies, a subscription-based announcement layer, and a reputation/confidence-weighted consensus layer so that scientific data artifacts can autonomously validate evidence, reconcile cross-institution contradictions, and update confidence after their publishing institutions disappear. An open Python reference implementation is evaluated on 4,305 rare-disease FDOs (ClinVar, HPO, Orphanet); the trimmed weighted-mean consensus resolves 56.3% of 3,914 expert-adjudicated ClinVar conflicts and degrades gracefully under Sybil, collusion, and poisoning attacks within its Byzantine bound (f < n/5). The work shows decision logic can live alongside the data artifact and stay auditable via provenance vocabularies, keeping FAIR data actionable beyond institutional continuity.

title: Portable Agent Memory: A Protocol for Cryptographically-Verified Memory Transfer Across Heterogeneous AI Agents
summary: Portable Agent Memory is an open protocol and Python SDK for exporting, transporting, and re-hydrating LLM-agent memory across heterogeneous models (Claude, GPT-4, Gemini, Llama) with cryptographic integrity. It models memory as five components, links entries in a Merkle-DAG provenance graph (BLAKE3 content-addressing + Ed25519 root signing) for tamper-evident lineage, adds capability-scoped access tokens with redaction/'right-to-be-forgotten' support, and an injection-resistant re-hydration pipeline. The data-management relevance is via provenance/lineage tracking, governance/access control, and integrity verification over agent-accumulated knowledge, exposed as MCP tools (pam_export_memory/pam_import_memory).

title: Beyond Manual Curation: Augmenting Targeted Protein Degradation Databases via Agentic Literature Extraction Workflows
summary: The paper presents an expert-in-the-loop, multi-agent LLM workflow that extracts structured targeted-protein-degradation (TPD) assay records from full-text papers and supplementary files to augment manually curated databases (MolGlueDB, PROTAC-DB). Three GPT-5 agents (Extractor, Analyst, Refiner) plus a semantic-matching module, driven by a cross-validated prompt-refinement module (CAPO) trained on only seven annotated papers, achieve record-level F1=0.98 and expand the databases by 81% and 92% with high expert-validated correctness. The work frames database curation as a domain-specific extraction task with a triangular evaluation (LLM predictions vs. baseline DB vs. expert ground truth) and releases the workflow, prompts, and datasets.

title: A categorical error sensitivity index (ISEC): A preventive ordinal decision-support measure for irrecoverable errors in manual data entry systems
summary: The paper introduces ISEC (Categorical Error Sensitivity Index), an automated ordinal metric that ranks pairs of nominal categories by their structural susceptibility to confusion in manual data-entry systems, aiming to prevent irrecoverable categorical errors that propagate into KPIs. It fuses semantic distance (word embeddings via a vector DB), a custom-weighted Damerau-Levenshtein morphological transformation cost, and empirical frequency, using ChromaDB/HNSW approximate nearest-neighbor search to cut complexity (~195x speedup over brute force). It is validated on three datasets (Argentine judicial records, retail SME inventory, synthetic ISO-1832 metalworking codes) as a preventive, pre-aggregation data-governance instrument for SMEs.

title: FSD50K-Solo: Automated Curation of Single-Source Sound Events
summary: FSD50K-Solo presents an automated data-curation framework that identifies and filters multi-source samples from the large FSD50K audio dataset to produce a clean single-source subset. It synthesizes clean single-class events with a diffusion model (Stable Audio Open), builds controlled noisy mixtures for supervision, and trains a BEATs-encoder + Bi-LSTM/MLP classifier to flag single- vs multi-source clips, achieving 95.51% accuracy on an expert-curated test set. The released FSD50K-Solo subset (32,880 samples) preserves more usable data (69.17%) than human-rating filtering (60.58%) while improving audio-quality scores.

title: Croissant Baker: Metadata Generation for Discoverable, Governable, and Reusable ML Datasets
summary: Croissant Baker is an open-source, local-first CLI that automatically generates validated Croissant (JSON-LD) metadata directly from a dataset directory, so governed/large repositories that cannot be uploaded to public platforms can still produce machine-checkable, discoverable, reusable metadata. It uses a deterministic four-stage pipeline (file discovery + SHA-256, format-aware handler dispatch, metadata/schema extraction, Croissant assembly + mlcroissant validation) with a typed handler registry covering CSV/Parquet/WFDB/DICOM/NIfTI/FHIR/JSON/image formats, evaluated on 140+ datasets (up to MIMIC-IV at 886M rows) with 97-100% agreement against producer-authored ground truth. It deliberately separates deterministic structural inference from CLI-supplied semantic fields, and sketches a future MCP-mediated LLM-agent extension that would propose semantic values under mandatory human review.

title: CitePrism: Human-in-the-Loop AI for Citation Auditing and Editorial Integrity
summary: CitePrism is a transparent hybrid decision-support prototype for manuscript-level citation auditing in editorial workflows, combining LLM-assisted contextual relevance scoring, embedding similarity, and metadata verification/enrichment (OpenAlex, Crossref, Semantic Scholar, arXiv) with mandatory human-analyst review. It enriches reference metadata, computes fused relevance scores, and surfaces integrity flags (metadata mismatch, missing DOI/abstract, retraction signals, questionable self-citation) as review prompts rather than automated verdicts. A single-manuscript pilot (104 pavement-engineering references) reached Cohen's kappa=0.429 and, at threshold tau=17, flagged all human-labeled irrelevant citations while producing false positives requiring analyst review.

title: Vidya: An AI-Driven Modular Pipeline for Archival Automation and Semantic Metadata Enrichment
summary: Vidya is a modular, LLM-orchestrated pipeline that automates archival ingestion and semantic metadata enrichment for digitized 'dark data' in memory institutions. It constrains LLM outputs using YAML-defined ontologies (Dublin Core, BIBO) and Pydantic validation (a 'digital straitjacket') to produce deterministic, standards-compliant JSON (NOBRADE, ISAD(G)), with an SQLite state machine, OCR quality gate, and automatic export to repositories like Omeka S, Tainacan, and DSpace. On a 50-document test set it reached ~85% enrichment accuracy and reduced multi-decade manual processing to days/weeks at low cost on modest hardware.

title: Automated Big Data Quality Assessment using Knowledge Graph Embeddings
summary: The paper proposes a knowledge-driven approach to automate big-data quality assessment by representing data-context characteristics, quality rules, and quality dimensions in a Neo4j knowledge graph, then using knowledge graph embeddings (AmpliGraph's FocusE, which injects numeric edge weights) to predict the links and weights between a new dataset's attributes and the relevant quality rules/dimensions, yielding a context-specific quality assessment plan. It improves on the authors' prior BIGQA context analyzer (Node2Vec + K-NN) by avoiding strict schema matching and covering all input attributes. Evaluated on a real-world Lebanese Atomic Energy Commission radiation-sensor dataset, the embedding approach produced a more complete assessment plan than BIGQA, with link-prediction metrics of Hits@10=0.66, MRR=0.19, MR=38.99.

title: KadiAssistant: A conversational AI Agent for information retrieval in Kadi4Mat
summary: KadiAssistant is a privacy-by-design conversational AI agent integrated into the Kadi4Mat research data repository that lets researchers retrieve, aggregate, and synthesize information from heterogeneous, access-controlled materials-science data. It uses a self-hosted LLM (gpt-oss-120B) with a LangGraph agentic state graph and three tools (semantic similarity search, record-metadata retrieval, record-connection retrieval) over a pgvector/HNSW vector store that respects Kadi4Mat's fine-grained access permissions. The authors demonstrate single- and multi-tool-call retrieval on three datasets, analyze k-NN/memory scaling to 1M vectors, and report hallucination and tool-completeness failure modes.

title: Ontological Knowledge Blocks: Executable Compliance and Profile-Based Validation for Trustworthy AI Systems
summary: Introduces Ontological Knowledge Blocks (OKBs), a programmable governance substrate that deterministically compiles human-reviewed regulatory obligations (YAML Intermediate Representation) into machine-checkable SHACL constraint shapes over RDF/OWL evidence graphs, with PROV-O provenance links binding AI decisions to model artifacts and usage logs. Governance profiles select and compose KB modules via set union, enabling profile-based reconfiguration without changing service code; two prototypes are evaluated on an AI-assisted HPC GPU-hour allocation scenario across 24 validation runs and four profiles. Results show profile-sensitive verdicts, strictly additive violation accumulation, sub-100ms median SHACL latency, and that the Combined profile is strictly the most comprehensive.

title: MetaboKG: An Analysis-centric Knowledge Graph Framework for Untargeted Metabolomics
summary: MetaboKG is an analysis-centric knowledge graph framework that integrates fragmented untargeted-metabolomics resources (spectra, features, annotations, confidence evidence, contextual metadata) from public repositories into a unified, provenance-aware semantic model grounded in PROV-O/SIO and aligned to MS, ChEBI, NCBITaxon, ENVO, and NCIT. It contributes a transformation/curation workflow that harmonizes Pan-ReDU metadata via semi-automated ontology term matching (OLS4 top-K, evaluated for accuracy) and regex compositional parsers, an LLM step to recover GNPS-job-to-MassIVE-dataset correspondences from 2,141 papers, and a Universal Annotation Identifier strategy for incremental ingestion and post hoc linkage. It was demonstrated at scale on 680 GNPS molecular-networking results and evaluated via SPARQL competency questions on biochemical enrichment, environmental specificity, and cross-instrument variation.

title: MimirRAG: A Multi-Agent RAG Framework for Financial Data Retrieval with Metadata Integration
summary: MimirRAG is a modular multi-agent RAG system for financial-document QA that pairs an automated ingest pipeline (Docling structure-preserving PDF parsing, table-aware chunking, and an LLM-based Extractor agent that pulls per-document metadata such as company, date, report type, and summary) with agentic retrieval (Planner, Search, Validator, Writer agents) over a LanceDB hybrid index, plus foreign-key linkage of chunks to source documents for traceability. An ablation shows metadata integration, table-aware chunking, and the agentic workflow are the three key enablers, reaching 89.3% on a 150-question FinanceBench subset; expert validation with four bank analysts surfaced needs for calibrated trust, comprehensive data integration, and personalization. The data-management contributions (automated metadata extraction, ingest/chunking, and provenance linkage) are central rather than incidental, justifying a keep.

title: Closing the Loop in Teleoperation: Episode-Level Data Quality Assessment and Feedback for High-Quality Demonstration Collection
summary: DQAF is a two-stage AI pipeline that assesses the quality of teleoperated robot demonstration episodes: a Vision-Language Model (Gemini Flash 1.5) infers semantic subtask progress while telemetry analysis computes execution-quality metrics (action saturation, motion smoothness, gripper chatter, stalling), and an LLM (Gemini 3 Pro) fuses these into an episode-level quality score plus actionable natural-language feedback. The goal is to filter/curate high-quality demonstration data at the source and reduce downstream manual data-curation burden, evaluated against a human reviewer on 100 episodes (85.7% failure-detection recall) and in a pilot user study where operators receiving automated feedback improved faster. It frames data-quality assessment as a closed loop during collection rather than post-hoc filtering.

title: Knowledge Graphs as the Missing Data Layer for LLM-Based Industrial Asset Operations
summary: The paper argues that for LLM-based industrial asset-operations agents, the data model behind the tools matters more than the LLM orchestration. It builds a typed knowledge graph from AssetOpsBench's document sources via an 8-step ETL pipeline (equipment hierarchy, sensors, failure-mode embeddings, events, dependency topology) and routes questions to three tiers: LLM-generated Cypher (65%->82-83% on the same GPT-4), deterministic native graph/optimization primitives (99%), and generation-augmented knowledge (GAK) that materializes missing facts as provenance-tagged graph nodes (tagged source:LLM-derived) before answering. The 'inverted LLM' pattern constrains the LLM to schema-grounded query generation or one-shot enrichment while the graph executes deterministically; on the expanded 467-scenario benchmark deterministic handlers reach 100% pass with 0.848 avg score.

title: Exploring Autonomous Agentic Data Engineering for Model Specialization
summary: The paper formalizes 'Autonomous Agentic Data Engineering,' a task in which an LLM agent independently executes the full training-data curation pipeline (strategy planning, prompt design, data synthesis via a fixed teacher model, validation, and iterative optimization) to specialize a fixed student model, measured by post-training performance gain. It evaluates One-Shot vs. closed-loop Iterative agents across Science, Code, and Finance, finding iterative feedback-driven curation yields large gains (GPT-5.2: +57.29% avg) and can surpass human-designed pipelines, while exposing failure modes around data quality assurance and quantity control. Contributions include a budget-controlled execution/evaluation environment with curation tools (check_submission, train_model, evaluate_dataset) and a performance-based scoring protocol.

title: Eywa: Provenance-Grounded Long-Term Memory for AI Agents
summary: Eywa is a provenance-grounded long-term memory architecture for AI agents that stores immutable source evidence before deriving canonical 'belief' facts, validates extracted facts against typed signals/hard anchors and source support, and retrieves bounded context through a deterministic, LLM-free multi-route read path, keeping every belief traceable to source evidence for audit, repair, and user erasure. It is evaluated on conversational-memory benchmarks (LoCoMo C1-C4 90.19% judge accuracy with Sonnet, LongMemEval-S 88.2%, BEAM 81.45% mean nugget). The data-management relevance comes from its provenance graph, lineage, data-validation, and right-to-erasure design applied to the memory substrate, though the substrate is agent memory rather than managed datasets.

title: When Helping Hurts and How to Fix It: Multi-Agent Debate for Data Cleaning
summary: This Meta study asks when multi-agent debate (a Generator proposing cleaning operations and an adversarial Critic challenging them) helps or hurts LLM-based data cleaning, evaluated across three benchmarks (AutoDCWorkflow generation, MMTU comprehension, MaTElDa detection), four model families, and 6,000+ task-condition pairs. It finds debate's effect reverses sign: it improves error detection (+27.4pp F1) but degrades open-ended generation (-1.6 to -15.5pp) via 'critique-induced confusion' (CIC), where the Generator uncritically accepts hallucinated Critic feedback and retracts correct operations. The authors derive a formal 'debate benefit condition' (debate helps when Critic verification odds weighted by fixability exceed Generator baseline accuracy odds), and show that pairing a code-execution-grounded Critic with evidence-gated generation yields the first debate config to significantly beat single-agent on a generative task (+5.3pp).

title: Powering An Ecosystem Of Pedagogical AI Agents: A Validation Strategy For A Unified Data Architecture
summary: This paper presents an empirical validation strategy for A4L 2.0, a cloud-native unified data architecture (the 'Data Engine 2.0' ingest/transform/pseudonymize/store layer) that manages high-volume event streams produced by an ecosystem of pedagogical AI agents (conversational assistants, coaches, SAMI social agents) plus learners and instructors. Using a two-stage black-box, architecture-based testing method across QA and production environments with synthetic and authentic 1EdTech Caliper/Edu-API event data, the team processed over 2.7M production requests and stress-tested schema validation, pseudonymization (privacy), referential integrity, data observability, and scalability. The data-management angle is the pipeline itself, with AI agents as the heterogeneous data sources; the work surfaces persistent privacy/governance and data-consistency failure modes rather than proposing autonomous agents that do data management.

title: JAVEDIT: Joint Audio-Visual Instruction-Guided Video Editing with Agentic Data Curation
summary: JAVEdit builds JAVEdit-100k, a 100K-triplet joint audio-visual video editing dataset, whose construction hinges on an 'Agent-in-the-loop' quality control system: an Orchestrator agent (Claude Opus) and Inspector agent (Gemini) form a closed loop that detects data-quality failures, classifies them hierarchically (systemic/modular/instance), patches pipeline code, retries, and stores verified fixes in a reusable Problem Pattern Library. Ablations show this agentic quality control raises the human-judged qualification rate of generated data from 36% to 83% and improves all downstream benchmark metrics versus a no-agent control set of equal size. The DM-relevant contribution is the autonomous, self-repairing agentic data-curation/quality-control pipeline used to construct and validate a large multimodal dataset.

title: The Violation Situation Pattern: A Knowledge-Graph Pattern for Compliance Violations
summary: The paper introduces the Violation Situation Pattern (VSP), an ontology design pattern that reifies each detected compliance violation in a legal knowledge graph as a persistent node carrying a rule identifier, temporal validity, a five-state review/remediation lifecycle, and PROV-O-aligned immutable transition events, so audit history becomes a graph traversal rather than a discarded query result. Four deontic compliance rules (unauthorized signature, expired mandate, missing confidentiality/breach-notification clauses) are operationalized via a deterministic FCL->Cypher->MERGE pipeline and evaluated against BODACC corporate-officer gazettes, 73 GDPRhub Article 33 enforcement decisions, and a SHACL cross-formalism portability check. The central finding is rule-body independence: detection logic can evolve (raising F1 from 0.312 to 0.602) without invalidating accumulated audit history.

title: Proof-Carrying Agent Actions: Model-Agnostic Runtime Governance for Heterogeneous Agent Systems
summary: The paper presents Proof-Carrying Agent Actions (PCAA), a runtime-neutral governance model that treats an 'action certificate' as the primary trust object for high-risk agent actions (e.g., publishing data externally) across heterogeneous agent runtimes.
