It targets the curation gap where extracted evidence stays siloed and non-reusable, and combines human review with automated labeling, concordance/conflict-resolution analytics, and programmatic R/Python API access. The paper is an introduction/overview with many user-contributed case studies (toxicology SDS extraction, clinical trials, COVID-19 SERs, ecology) rather than a controlled benchmark.

title: Transforming Data Annotation with AI Agents: A Review of Architectures, Reasoning, Applications, and Impact
summary: This is a review surveying how LLM-powered AI agents are transforming data annotation, addressing longstanding challenges of scalability, consistency, cost, and limited domain expertise. It analyzes agent architectures, reasoning strategies, workflow integration patterns, evaluation methods, and real-world applications across healthcare, finance, technology, and media, while covering tools/platforms and concerns like quality assurance, bias, and transparency. It outlines future directions including federated learning, cross-modal reasoning, and responsible system design.

title: Conceptual service architecture to synchronise research data management services using machine-actionable data management plans
summary: This paper proposes a conceptual service architecture that uses machine-actionable data management plans (maDMPs) to automatically exchange and synchronize DMP information across semi-automated research data management services representing different stakeholders, so that DMPs stay current throughout the research lifecycle rather than becoming static, obsolete documents. The architecture is specified via UML and BPMN views (physical, development, logical, process) and instantiated by a prototype service connecting a data repository to a DMP tool. It evaluates how well the defined processes keep DMP contents up to date and what criteria are needed for high automation, feeding into RDA maDMP standardization discussions.

title: Designing an architecture for machine-actionable research data management planning in an institutional context
summary: This TU Wien thesis tackles the data-management-planning stage by moving from static DMPs to machine-actionable DMPs (maDMPs) that can automatically integrate information and update themselves. It proposes a system architecture embedded in an institution's research-data-management infrastructure, modeled with BPMN and ArchiMate, and introduces a 'Service Broker' that discovers, configures, and provisions ICT services during planning; a proof-of-concept at TU Wien shows maDMP workflows can be semi-automated and serialized per the RDA DMP Common Standard. Evaluation finds maDMPs cannot fully replace conventional DMPs on completeness/expressiveness but extend them with machine actionability.

title: Benchmarking for Keyword Extraction Methodologies in Maintenance Work Orders
summary: This PHM Society paper benchmarks two approaches for turning unstructured, jargon- and error-filled maintenance work order (MWO) text into computable structured data: a labor-intensive rules-based expert system (keyword spotting) versus a data-driven, human-in-the-loop tagging GUI that ranks tokens by TF-IDF and prompts an expert to classify them as Problem, Solution, or Item. On a public 5485-record mining-shovel dataset, both methods are compared via survival analysis (Kaplan-Meier and Weibull MTTF estimates) across major subsystems, with multi-tag approximations matching rules-based estimates to within ~1 day. The authors conclude neither method clearly wins and advocate a hybrid pipeline where ML-discovered latent patterns seed taxonomies/ontologies that human experts then refine via rule definitions.

title: Machine-actionable data management plans (maDMPs)
summary: This 2017 IDCC workshop report (47 participants from 16 countries) synthesizes community-generated use cases for machine-actionable data management plans (maDMPs) across eight topics: interoperability, persistent identifiers, institutional and repository use cases, data discovery/reuse, evaluation/monitoring, disciplinary tailoring, and publishing. The central argument is that DMPs should move from static documents to machine-actionable hubs that automate metadata population, repository recommendation, notifications/reporting, compliance and quality checks, and provenance linking via PIDs and a common data model. It articulates consensus on the need for a common maDMP standard and proposes an RDA working group to develop one.

title: Data Management Plans and Linked Open Data: exploiting machine actionable data management plans through Open Science Graphs
summary: This work explores machine-actionable Data Management Plans (maDMPs) and their integration with Linked Open Data through Open Science Graphs, aiming to make DMP content machine-readable and interlinkable across research-data infrastructures. It targets the planning and metadata stages of the data-management lifecycle by leveraging semantic/linked-data representations to automate DMP exploitation. Based on title and metadata only (no abstract or PDF available), the contribution centers on standards-based automation rather than a demonstrated AI-agent system.

title: Towards semantic representation of machine-actionable Data Management Plans
summary: This 2020 work proposes a semantic (likely RDF/ontology-based) representation for machine-actionable Data Management Plans (maDMPs), enabling DMP content to be processed and exchanged automatically by tools rather than read only as prose. It targets the planning stage of the data-management lifecycle, supporting automation and interoperability of DMP information across systems. Assessment is metadata-only as no abstract or PDF was available.

title: Research Object Crates and Machine-actionable Data Management Plans
summary: A 2020 contribution (Fachrepositorium Lebenswissenschaften) on combining Research Object Crates (RO-Crate) with machine-actionable Data Management Plans (maDMPs). The work concerns making data-management planning and associated metadata machine-readable and automatable so that DMP information can be packaged, exchanged, and acted upon by tooling. No abstract or full text was available, so the assessment rests on the title and venue.

title: Automating Corpora Generation with Semantic Cleaning and Tagging of Tweets for Multi-dimensional Social Media Analytics
summary: This 2015 paper automates the construction of clean text corpora from streaming tweets to support multi-dimensional social media analytics. The 'processTweet' pipeline ingests tweets, extracts and structures metadata (location, retweet/follower counts), performs semantic cleaning (slang/abbreviation correction via lexicons, phonetic matching with Metaphone, splitting joined words via dynamic programming), and tags/learns domain entities to build and enhance a domain knowledge base. Tested on Indian-politics tweets, it reached 85.55% accuracy in domain-term identification, with required human intervention dropping to ~18% as the KB matured.

title: Potential of natural language processing for metadata extraction from environmental scientific publications
summary: This paper evaluates three classical NLP techniques (LDA topic modeling, tailored regular expressions, and spaCy shortest-dependency-path relationship extraction) to automatically extract structured metadata (coordinates, soil texture, soil type, rainfall, disk diameter, tensions) and driver-variable relationships from environmental/soil-science publications, aiming to support semi-automated evidence synthesis and meta-database construction. Applied to two soil-science corpora (OTIM, 172 source pubs; Meta, 1469 abstracts), regex+dictionary extraction reached precision 0.83-1.00 and recall 0.56-1.00, while relationship classification was correct in ~66% of cases. The authors conclude NLP can prefill curated databases for human verification but cannot replace human supervision, and point to transformer/BERT-based methods as the future direction.

title: Workshop Report - Research Data Lifecycle And Machine-Actionable Data Management Plans
summary: A 2017 RDA workshop report from the DMP Common Standards WG that gathered stakeholder requirements for machine-actionable Data Management Plans (maDMPs), mapped to the research data lifecycle. It frames how DMPs can move from static documents to structured, automatable artifacts that systems can act on, laying groundwork for later DMP tooling and automation. It is an early, foundational planning-stage piece rather than an implemented AI-agent solution.

title: Ten Simple Rules For Machine-Actionable Data Management Plans (Preprint)
summary: This paper presents ten simple rules for putting machine-actionable Data Management Plans (maDMPs) into practice, transforming DMPs from free-form administrative text into structured, machine-readable artifacts that can be automatically generated, exchanged, and embedded across research tools and systems. The goal is to reduce administrative burden and improve information quality by enabling automated population and sharing of DMP content among researchers, funders, repositories, and administrators. It is a foundational best-practices/recommendations paper underpinning much subsequent maDMP tooling and automation work.

title: Enhancing the Benefits of Machine-Actionable DMPs with Generative AI
summary: A California Digital Library talk on using large language models to help review, write, and improve connections within machine-actionable data management plans (maDMPs), while keeping the human author as the final authority. It reports on ongoing CDL initiatives to increase the benefits of and ease the burden of writing DMPs, sharing learnings, progress, and tips for others working in the same space.

title: Enhancing the Benefits of Machine-Actionable DMPs with Generative AI
summary: A talk from the California Digital Library on applying large language models to help review, write, and improve connections within machine-actionable data management plans (maDMPs), aiming to reduce the burden of DMP authoring while keeping the human author as the final authority. It shares CDL's ongoing initiatives, learnings, and practical tips for others working on AI-assisted DMP tooling.

title: Utilizing the Argos machine actionable DMP and OpenAIRE knowledge graph to understand, drive, and assess FAIR adoption across CoMeCT partners
summary: A CoMeCT meeting presentation describing how machine-actionable DMPs built with the Argos platform are aggregated via APIs into the OpenAIRE Knowledge Graph to drive and assess FAIR adoption across clinical trial and cohort partners. By making data-collection, governance, standards, and access information machine-readable from project start, it enables a dynamic knowledge graph of study relationships that surfaces interoperability gaps and alignment opportunities. It frames iterative maDMP updates plus OpenAIRE monitoring as a mechanism for continuous FAIR assessment, though it describes structured-metadata automation rather than AI agents.

title: Utilizing the Argos machine actionable DMP and OpenAIRE knowledge graph to understand, drive, and assess FAIR adoption across CoMeCT partners
summary: A conference presentation describing how machine-actionable data management plans (maDMPs) built with the Argos platform are aggregated via APIs into the OpenAIRE Knowledge Graph to drive and assess FAIR data adoption across the CoMeCT trial and cohort partners. By making data collection, governance, standards, and access conditions machine-readable early in a project, the approach builds a dynamic knowledge graph of study relationships to surface interoperability gaps and alignment opportunities and to enable continuous, iterative monitoring of FAIR implementation.

title: Framing the scope of the common data model for machine-actionable Data Management Plans
summary: This RDA DMP Common Standards working-group paper frames the scope of a common data model for machine-actionable Data Management Plans (maDMPs), which let systems act on behalf of researchers rather than relying on static, manually-implemented text DMPs. It reports consultations and proof-of-concept tools to identify stakeholder information needs, define a model for exchanging DMP information between systems, and identify the infrastructure services/components needed to automate data-management tasks. It is a foundational standardization/automation effort underpinning much subsequent maDMP tooling.

title: Machine-actionable DMP application (DMap)
summary: DMap is a research prototype/demo tool that automates the workflow of writing machine-actionable Data Management Plans (maDMPs), guiding researchers through project, staff, data, license and repository selection. It implements the RDA DMP Common Standard exchange model so DMPs become machine-actionable rather than static documents. It targets the planning stage of the data-management lifecycle, automating DMP creation instead of relying on AI agents.

title: Machine-Actionable Data Management Plans (Madmps): Idcc17 Workshop Materials
summary: Workshop materials from the IDCC17 session on machine-actionable data management plans (maDMPs), held in Edinburgh as part of the 12th International Digital Curation Conference. The materials gather community-generated use cases across eight stakeholder topics and articulate a consensus on the need for a common standard to make DMPs machine-actionable, enabling future automated tooling and services. It is a foundational, community-consensus artifact (slides plus an accompanying RIO Journal report) rather than a built system, benchmark, or evaluation.

title: Machine-Actionable DMPs in the Repository: Motivation and Implementation
summary: A conference session and case study on implementing machine-actionable Data Management Plans (maDMPs) inside the Haplo Repository, using the RDA Common Standard to convert siloed, unstructured DMP PDFs into a structured, machine-actionable data model alongside dataset deposit. It discusses mapping institutional and funder forms to the maDMP model, the challenges of doing so, and quick wins versus longer-term benefits of repository-integrated DMPs. There is no AI agent or LLM involved; it is classical structured-data automation of the DMP planning workflow.

title: D5.5 Actionable Modular Data Management for brokering distributed resources
summary: EOSC-Nordic deliverable D5.5 reports on adding support for machine-actionable Data Management Plans (maDMPs) to four different DMP tools, enabling actionable, modular data management for brokering distributed resources. It documents applications of the maDMP standard and lessons learned from the implementations. The work targets the planning/DMP lifecycle stage via machine-readable, interoperable plans that can drive automated data-management workflows.

title: Turning Machine-Actionable DMPs Into FAIR Digital Objects
summary: A short conceptual extended abstract proposing how machine-actionable Data Management Plans (maDMPs) could evolve to be compatible with the FAIR Digital Object (FDO) architecture, either by pointing to FDOs or by becoming FDOs themselves with defined types and operations. It also sketches an ecosystem shift in which DMP tools evolve into maDMP stores acting as repository/registry systems and communicating via the DOIP protocol, enabling more automated RDM tasks and novel FAIRness-based DMP assessment. No system is implemented or evaluated; the goal is to gather community feedback and prioritize next steps.

title: Application Profile for Machine-Actionable Data Management Plans
summary: This paper presents the Research Data Alliance's official recommendation for an application profile for machine-actionable Data Management Plans (maDMPs), allowing information traditionally captured in free-text DMPs to be expressed in a structured, machine-actionable form. It describes the consensus-driven methodology behind the profile, key design decisions, and systems that have adopted it. The standard is foundational infrastructure for automating data-management planning and for tools/agents that create, exchange, or act on DMP information.

title: Interconnecting Systems Using Machine-Actionable Data Management Plans – Hackathon Report
summary: Reports on an RDA hackathon where 89 participants from 21 countries explored the common standard for machine-actionable Data Management Plans (maDMPs), which enables automatic exchange, integration, and validation of DMP information. Work covered integrating tools and services, mapping funder templates, and developing new serialisations of the maDMP standard. It is a community/automation effort around the data-management planning lifecycle stage rather than an AI-agent system.

title: Data Management Plans: Implications for Automated Analyses
summary: This study compares an automated text-analysis approach against a manual scorecard for evaluating 21 funded research-project Data Management Plans (DMPs) against open-research best practices. The automated method reliably surfaced terms for availability, metadata, and sharing and produced less granular but similar conclusions to manual review, more efficiently. The authors recommend ways to make both DMP exercises and automated analysis more useful, pointing toward machine-actionable, structured DMPs.

title: Towards a Toolbox for Automated Assessment of Machine-Actionable Data Management Plans
summary: This paper explores methods to automate the assessment of machine-actionable Data Management Plans (maDMPs), addressing the bottleneck that DMP review is time-consuming and requires scarce data-stewardship expertise. It proposes a toolbox that goes beyond human-readable reports to provide automated pre-assessment and to fetch supplementary information, mapping the identified automation methods to various reviewer goals. The work is conceptual/method-mapping rather than a deployed agent system.

title: Making Data Management Plans Machine Actionable: Templates and Tools
summary: A practice paper from the EOSC Nordic T5.3.2 task group surveying tools and templates for creating machine-actionable Data Management Plans (maDMPs) compliant with the RDA DMP Common Standard (RDCS). It details the Stockholm University SU-VR template in DMP Online (multiple-choice questionnaires, JSON->XML->XSLT->JSON conversion, Schematron-based FAIR assessment) and compares DSW, EasyDMP, Argos OpenAIRE, DAMAP, DMPTool, FIP2DMP, and SND projects, focusing on machine-actionability, RDCS compliance, integration with research information systems, and semi-automated DMP review. The work is document-engineering automation (validation, transformation, prefilling via APIs) rather than AI agents.

title: Automating Data Quality Validation for Dynamic Data Ingestion
summary: This EDBT 2021 paper addresses automating data-quality validation for dynamic (continuously ingested) data, where data and its expected properties shift over time and static rules go stale. Based on the title it proposes an automation approach that adapts quality checks to evolving incoming data during ingestion. No abstract or PDF was available, so details of the method, evaluation, and findings could not be verified.

title: Toolchain for Dataset Description with Contextual Recommendation from Machine-Actionable Data Management Plans
summary: This position paper proposes a toolchain that automates and enhances metadata description for research data by leveraging structured, machine-actionable data management plan content from RDMO (Research Data Management Organiser). It draws on project information, measurement equipment, sensors, and simulations to provide context-aware suggestions for metadata fields, aiming to reduce researcher burden and improve metadata quality and consistency in support of FAIR principles.

title: Análise de Hiperparâmetros em Aplicações de Aprendizado Profundo por meio de Dados de Proveniência
summary: CNNProv extends the DfAnalyzer dataflow tool to capture and analyze provenance data during deep-learning (CNN) training, adopting the W3C PROV standard so hyperparameter-derivation relationships are represented in a standardized, interoperable, queryable form rather than a proprietary one. Provenance is captured asynchronously by code instrumentation and stored in a MonetDB columnar database, with query and dataflow-visualization interfaces letting users analyze hyperparameter configurations at runtime. A case study on AlexNet/TensorFlow with the OxfordFlower17 dataset showed runtime queries (e.g., loss and elapsed time per epoch) were feasible with negligible capture overhead (at most ~4%).

title: The case for machine-actionable data management plans in ELIXIR
summary: This F1000Research poster/position piece argues that traditional Data Management Plans are treated as static, bureaucratic text documents and proposes the concept of Machine-Actionable DMPs (maDMPs) that remain human-readable while becoming machine-processable. It calls for the ELIXIR life-sciences infrastructure to host an open, distributed environment offering templates and services to create, share, reuse, and automatically process maDMPs in support of FAIR data principles. It is a proposal/challenge rather than an implemented or evaluated system.

title: Machine actionable DMPs in practice
summary: A Chalmers University poster describing a production implementation of machine-actionable Data Management Plans (maDMPs). Using the Data Stewardship Wizard with a custom maDMP REST API, they auto-create and auto-populate DMPs from funder/CRIS systems (SweCRIS, CORDIS, GDP) and automatically connect stakeholders (data protection office, storage, Swedish National Data Service) to relevant parts of the planning-to-preservation lifecycle, flagging personal/sensitive data and large storage needs early. The goal is to reduce the tedium of DMP writing while producing controlled, reusable metadata for FAIR data.

title: Automated Metadata Generation for Linked Data Generation and Publishing Workflows
summary: This 2016 LDOW paper presents an approach to automatically and incrementally generate provenance and other metadata throughout the Linked Data generation and publishing workflow, driven by declarative descriptions of RML mapping rules and data-source access interfaces. It defines which provenance/metadata properties (PROV-O, VoID, DCAT) to capture at each workflow step and at different granularities (dataset, named-graph, partition, triple, and RDF-term levels), and implements it by extending the RMLEditor and RMLProcessor tool chain. The 'agent' notion is the PROV-O person-vs-software-agent distinction rather than an AI agent, and the automation is classical/rule-based.

title: Machine actionable DMPs for the Research Data Repository
summary: A 2019 AGU Fall Meeting abstract describing machine-actionable Data Management Plans (maDMPs) integrated with a research data repository, aimed at automating the flow between DMP content and repository ingest/curation. With no abstract or PDF text available, only the title grounds the analysis: it addresses the planning stage of the data lifecycle via structured, machine-readable DMPs rather than a documented AI-agent architecture.

title: Exploring Machine-Actionable Data Management Plans.
summary: A short IEEE TCDL bulletin piece exploring machine-actionable Data Management Plans (maDMPs), i.e., representing DMP content in structured, machine-readable form so systems can act on it automatically rather than treating DMPs as static prose documents. Only the title is available (no abstract or full text), so specifics on architecture, evaluation, and findings cannot be grounded. The work sits in the data-management planning lifecycle stage and is automation-adjacent (maDMP tooling) rather than an LLM-agent system.
